summary: Invalidate the page cache on a price change; the store write must come first because cache misses refill from the store, a reason found only in the incident note.

required_facts.text: Delete the cache entry only after the store write, because a reader that misses the cache refills it from the store and would re-cache the old price.
also_matching: Delete the cache entry after the store write: a miss refills the cache from the store, so deleting first would re-cache the old price.
Write the store first, then invalidate; otherwise a page view in between caches the old price again for 24 hours.
Order matters: invalidating before the write lets a reader repopulate the cache with the stale price.
Invalidate only after store.put, or a concurrent page view could put the previous price back in the cache for a day.

forbidden_claims.text: The CDN caches product pages, which is why old prices were shown.
anchors: re:(?<!not )(?<!n't )\b(caused by|because of|due to|comes from|came from|blame on) (the )?(cdn|edge)
not_matching: The CDN does not cache price fragments (they are no-store); the stale prices came from our page cache.
Not caused by the CDN: price fragments are served with Cache-Control: no-store.
The CDN was ruled out; the old price came from our own page cache.
The CDN never caches price fragments, so only our page cache needs invalidating.
